html:
Fernando Botero was a Colombian painter and sculptor famous for his round, swollen figures of people and animals. He was the best-known artist from Latin America in his lifetime.

Born in Medellín, he studied in Spain and Italy and lived mostly in Europe and New York. His style, which he called volume, enlarged bodies to give them weight and sensuality, often with gentle humour about the middle class, priests and generals of Colombia.

He also painted the violence of his country, including the death of Pablo Escobar, and in 2005 the abuse of prisoners at Abu Ghraib in Iraq. He gave large collections of his own work and of other masters to museums in Bogotá and Medellín, where his bronze sculptures fill a public square. He died in Monaco in 2023.
